items.stem: Why is net present value generally preferred to simple payback?

options.text: NPV accounts for the time value of money and all project cash flows, not just the time to recover outlay
options.rationale: Correct: payback ignores timing beyond recovery and later cash flows.

options.text: NPV is always easier to calculate
options.rationale: NPV is usually more, not less, involved.

options.text: Payback cannot be computed for most projects

options.rationale: NPV is built from cash flows.

items.explanation: Correct: payback ignores timing beyond recovery and later cash flows.

items.stem: Which TWO cash flows are relevant to a project investment decision? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An opportunity cost of using space the project occupies
options.rationale: Correct: forgone use is a relevant cost.

options.text: Market research already paid for last year
options.rationale: That is a sunk cost and irrelevant.

options.text: An unchanged head-office cost reallocated to the project

items.stem: A project has a positive NPV but a payback longer than the company's informal rule of thumb. The best response is to:

options.text: Weigh the positive NPV and strategic value against liquidity needs rather than reject on payback alone
options.rationale: Correct: payback is a crude screen; NPV and context should lead.

options.text: Reject it automatically because of payback
options.rationale: A rigid payback rule can destroy value.

options.text: Accept it without any further thought
options.rationale: Liquidity and risk still warrant judgement.
Manipulating the number is not appraisal.
